name: Gilt market
summary: Gilt yields rise after the Bank of England's first rate rise since 2023 on 5 Nov
state: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov on an 8–1 vote, its first rise in three years, and gilt yields rose, led by two-year bonds (Euronext); traders added to bets on a December hike (Bloomberg). The 10-year yield had fallen to 5.14% on 4 Nov, a two-month low and below its mid-October multi-year high (Trading Economics). No weak auction or BoE intervention has been reported.
for_you: Higher gilt yields feed through to fixed-rate mortgage pricing and government borrowing costs.
rubric_hit: Long gilts near multi-decade highs = Watch; 10y 1m move < 40bp

sources.title: Euronext — Bank of England delivers first rate hike in three years, gilt yields rise
Bloomberg — BoE rate-hike odds rise as markets price in December move

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
